Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

The competent Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the company's registered office, coordinated nationally through the Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central).

Governing statute

Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), particularly Articles 4, 19-23, 28-32, 43-55, 61-63, 159-197, 210-241, and 278; Law 18/2022 on the Creation and Growth of Companies, including its amendments to minimum capital and formation procedures; Commercial Registry Regulations approved by Royal Decree 1784/1996.

Formation / constitutional filings

Notarial public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución) filed with the competent Provincial Commercial Registry, together with the prescribed registration application and tax identification documentation.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 67 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

The statutory minimum capital for a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. Until the capital reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve until the reserve plus capital reaches EUR 3,000, and shareholders have supplementary liability for the difference between EUR 3,000 and the subscribed capital in specified liquidation circumstances. A separate escrow account is not generally mandatory; a bank deposit certificate may be used, although the founders may instead assume joint responsibility for the accuracy of the contribution under Article 62 of the Companies Act.

Funding & unlock path: Before occupying premises, obtain the applicable municipal activity or opening authorization and satisfy fire-safety requirements under the Spanish Building Technical Code and, where applicable, Royal Decree 2267/2004 on fire safety in industrial establishments. Structural load and installation inspections are required where the premises are altered or equipment is installed. Comply with Law 31/1995 on Occupational Risk Prevention, including risk assessment, emergency planning, worker training, health surveillance where appropriate, and coordination with external prevention services. Additional acoustic or fire inspections may apply to recording and dubbing studios.

Paid-in capital rule: The statutory minimum capital for a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. Until the capital reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve until the reserve plus capital reaches EUR 3,000, and shareholders have supplementary liability for the difference between EUR 3,000 and the subscribed capital in specified liquidation circumstances. A separate escrow account is not generally mandatory; a bank deposit certificate may be used, although the founders may instead assume joint responsibility for the accuracy of the contribution under Article 62 of the Companies Act.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
RESOLVED, that the Company accepts the subscription and full payment of its issued share capital by [Founder Name], as recorded in the deed of incorporation. RESOLVED, that the registered office is adopted at [Full Spanish Address], with authority to update the address in the Commercial Registry when legally required. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed sole director for the statutory term, with the powers permitted by law and the articles of association, and is authorized to obtain the Company’s tax identification number, open bank accounts, execute filings, and complete all incorporation, employment, licensing, and operational formalities. The resolution is approved and signed by the attending shareholder(s) and director.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Exempted / Not Required

Not applicable for ordinary professional translation, localization, subtitling, and media-dubbing services. The relevant municipality may require an activity declaration or operating authorization for the premises. The competent autonomous-community industrial authority may become relevant only if the business installs regulated industrial equipment or operates a facility subject to sector-specific rules.

Category: No sector-specific manufacturing or industrial operating permit is ordinarily required. Depending on the premises and municipality, the applicable instrument may be a municipal responsible declaration for commencement of activity (declaración responsable de inicio de actividad) or a municipal activity and opening license.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es). In the Basque Country and Navarra the devolved Foral Haciendas administer corporate income tax, but AEAT retains exclusive national competence for VAT, customs, and excise duties.

E-government filing portal

1) Execute the SL incorporation deed before a Spanish notary, with the managing director already holding a Spanish NIE; 2) submit the census filing (Form 036 - Declaración censal) to AEAT, providing shareholder and manager details, the CNAE/ISIC 7490 activity code, and the registered office, which generates the provisional NIF; 3) register the company in the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) within one month of incorporation; 4) upon certification of the registry inscription, AEAT converts the provisional NIF into the definitive CIF/NIF (letter plus eight digits plus control character, format N-12345678-0) through a supplementary Form 036 filing; 5) the VAT identification (NIF-IVA) and the IAE municipal business tax registration are embedded in the same census declaration; 6) non-resident shareholders must obtain NIF-N (foreign legal entity) or NIE (foreign individual), appoint a fiscal representative with power of attorney when required, and present apostilled foreign documents accompanied by an official sworn translation into Spanish.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation - a Spanish SL is an opaque resident corporate taxpayer subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (IS) on worldwide income; the standard IS rate is 25% in mainland Spain, reduced to 15% for newly created entities with positive net equity in their first two tax periods (art. 29.1 LIS), with a 4% IS rate available to ZEC-qualifying entities in the Canary Islands and a 19% dividend/interest withholding generally applicable to non-resident shareholders under the Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR). No territorial or remittance-based carve-out applies to a resident SL. — 1) Execute the SL incorporation deed before a Spanish notary, with the managing director already holding a Spanish NIE; 2) submit the census filing (Form 036 - Declaración censal) to AEAT, providing shareholder and manager details, the CNAE/ISIC 7490 activity code, and the registered office, which generates the provisional NIF; 3) register the company in the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) within one month of incorporation; 4) upon certification of the registry inscription, AEAT converts the provisional NIF into the definitive CIF/NIF (letter plus eight digits plus control character, format N-12345678-0) through a supplementary Form 036 filing; 5) the VAT identification (NIF-IVA) and the IAE municipal business tax registration are embedded in the same census declaration; 6) non-resident shareholders must obtain NIF-N (foreign legal entity) or NIE (foreign individual), appoint a fiscal representative with power of attorney when required, and present apostilled foreign documents accompanied by an official sworn translation into Spanish.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation - a Spanish SL is an opaque resident corporate taxpayer subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (IS) on worldwide income; the standard IS rate is 25% in mainland Spain, reduced to 15% for newly created entities with positive net equity in their first two tax periods (art. 29.1 LIS), with a 4% IS rate available to ZEC-qualifying entities in the Canary Islands and a 19% dividend/interest withholding generally applicable to non-resident shareholders under the Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR). No territorial or remittance-based carve-out applies to a resident SL.

Available election forms

Spain has no check-the-box or pass-through election: an SL is permanently opaque, with no US-style entity classification election. Applicable statutory options include: (i) group taxation under the consolidated fiscal regime (LIS arts. 58-64) where direct/indirect control of 75% or more exists, elected through the corresponding tax-group census filing with AEAT; (ii) the automatic 15% reduced IS rate for qualifying newly created entities; (iii) the ETVE holding regime (art. 21 LIS) when the SL qualifies as a foreign-securities holding entity; (iv) the patent/innovation box allowing a 60% exemption of qualifying intangible income (art. 23 LIS); and (v) VAT grouping (grupo de entidades) for established Spanish group members. Hybrid mismatch rules transposing ATAD 2 (art. 15 LIS as amended by Ley 4/2021) override any cross-border mismatch election and invalidate double-deduction or deduction-without-inclusion structures.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No general SME exemption or VAT registration threshold exists: any person commencing commercial, professional, or artistic activities must file Form 036/037 and obtain the NIF-IVA before the first supply, regardless of expected turnover or loss position; Spain has not transposed the EU cross-border small-business exemption into Ley 37/1992, and the simplified 'módulos' regime covers only listed retail, agriculture, and artisan activities, never professional localization services. In practice, the first B2B invoice triggers compulsory VAT registration.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Physical export of goods: 0% export exemption under art. 21.1 Ley 37/1992 when a customs export declaration (DUA/Documento Único Administrativo) is accepted by AEAT customs and the goods physically leave the EU customs territory, evidenced by customs MRN status codes; goods must exit within the customs-supervised outward movement window (ordinarily 90 days from declaration acceptance, extendable with customs authorization). Localization services (translation, interpretation, subtitling, dubbing, transcreation) are services, not goods exports: zero-rating does not apply; instead the place-of-supply rules (arts. 69-70 LIVA) determine non-taxability as follows: (i) B2B services supplied to a customer established outside Spain are outside Spanish VAT scope, EU customers being subject to reverse charge with VIES VAT-number validation and non-EU customers bearing no Spanish VAT; (ii) B2C electronically supplied services (digital subtitle/master files) are deemed supplied at the consumer's location, so intra-EU consumer sales must be reported through the OSS (One-Stop-Shop) at destination-country VAT, with optional use of the EUR 10,000 intra-EU annual small-business threshold; (iii) input VAT attributable to non-taxable offshore services is recoverable only on a pro-rata basis (art. 104 LIVA) and, if the SL is not the exporter of goods, no customs export bundle applies to pure remote services.

  • Customs Export Declaration (DUA/Documento Único Administrativo) with MRN and customs exit status, lodged through AEAT's customs single window (Ventanilla Única Aduanera) or EDIFACT channel
  • Transportation and shipping evidence - Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or signed CMR as applicable, proving physical cross-border exit from EU territory
  • Commercial invoice incorporating INCOTERM, HS code, and the express clause 'exempt export - art. 21 Ley 37/1992' for goods, or for intra-EU supplies the VAT-registration references and 'reverse charge' indication
  • Inward Remittance Certificate from the payment rail (SWIFT MT103/MT202, Wise_B2B payout record, or Payoneer statement) evidencing receipt of foreign-currency export proceeds, adopting the 180-day inward-remittance compliance standard
  • Place-of-supply service documentation for localization work - signed localization/LMA contract, service acceptance certificate (dubbing QC report or translation delivery record), VIES validation printout for EU counterparties, and official sworn translation into Spanish where required
  • Ancillary media-delivery export file when physical deliverables (hard drives, master tapes, reference DVDs) are shipped, including packing list, freight forwarder receipt, and customs exit proof, archived with AEAT for the full 4-year limitation period

Mandatory B2B electronic invoicing is being phased in under Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece), with the implementing decree expected to require large undertakings (turnover over EUR 8,000,000) to issue, transmit, and receive structured e-invoices within one year of its approval and all other businesses within two years (expected compliance window 2025-2026); large enterprises and VAT groups subject to the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) must transmit invoice-issue and invoice-receipt records to AEAT via authenticated web services/API within 4 working days, with the extension to 8 calendar days for several record types, using XML/Facturae or EDIFACT formats; 'Verifactu' (RD 1007/2023 and Ley 11/2021 anti-fraud legislation) requires certified billing software that generates an immutable, hashed invoice record (Registro de Facturación), QR verification codes, and tamper-evident digital files; the Basque Country imposes the TicketBAI digital-stamping regime; invoices to Spanish public authorities must be submitted to the FACE portal as signed Facturae XML.

AEAT has a 4-year statutory assessment period (art. 66 LGT). Wrongful zero-rating or export exemption is prosecuted as 'obtención indebida de devoluciones' and 'infracción por dejar de ingresar' under arts. 191-193 LGT, with proportional penalties ranging from 50% for simple negligence up to 150% for concealment or fraudulent documentation, plus late-payment interest computed at the statutory rate and retrospective VAT clawback recomputed at 21% over the full invoiced consideration. Failure to produce the customs DUA or exit proof automatically disqualifies the 0% rate and recharacterizes the supply as standard-rated. Fabrication of export documentation may trigger criminal tax evasion under art. 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000, carrying imprisonment and fines. AEAT cross-border service audits combine the Verifactu/SII electronic invoice records with FX rail statements (Wise_B2B, Payoneer) to verify end-to-end traceability of exported services, and the burden of proof rests on the taxable person to substantiate the offshore destination and receipt of funds within the documented period.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain uses the euro and benefits from full current-account and capital-account convertibility under European Union law. There is no general Spanish exchange control, capital repatriation restriction, or requirement to obtain prior approval for ordinary inbound equity, intercompany loans, service receipts, dividends, interest, royalties, or liquidation proceeds. Transfers remain subject to bank identification, beneficial-owner verification, sanctions screening, anti-money-laundering controls, tax compliance, transfer-pricing support, and documentary evidence of the underlying transaction. Dividend, interest, royalty, and service remittances may trigger Spanish withholding-tax, treaty, beneficial-ownership, anti-abuse, or reporting analysis. Certain foreign investments may require ex post or prior declarations, and exceptional foreign-investment screening can apply to protected sectors or qualifying investors; a multilingual localization agency ordinarily falls outside protected-sector restrictions unless its facts create a regulated technology, defense, critical-infrastructure, or sensitive-data nexus.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain has no general statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, mandatory repatriation rule, compulsory conversion ratio, or fixed deadline for converting foreign-currency export receipts into euros. Export and service proceeds may generally remain in foreign-currency accounts or be converted at the company's discretion. Banks may request invoices, contracts, delivery evidence, customer identification, tax information, and payment-purpose data. Cross-border transactions may be reportable through Banco de España statistical-information systems or other regulatory channels depending on transaction type, resident status, amount, financial institution reporting, and applicable filing rules. Export receivables should be reconciled to accounting records, VAT treatment, customer invoices, and transfer-pricing documentation.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the Eurosystem and subject to applicable European Union payment-services, anti-money-laundering, capital-movement, and financial-markets rules.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Wise Fit: High

Medium to High for payment collection, supplier payments, foreign-currency wallets, and routine cross-border transfers, provided the provider is an authorized European Economic Area payment institution or electronic-money institution, or operates lawfully through passporting or an approved local arrangement. Wise Business, Payoneer, and comparable providers should be used only within their licensed product scope. They are not substitutes for a Spanish operating bank where a local corporate IBAN, statutory capital deposit, payroll, tax direct debit, cash services, bank guarantees, commercial lending, or enhanced documentary review is required. Client funds must not be commingled with company funds, and the company must not provide regulated payment, money-remittance, deposit-taking, or foreign-exchange services to third parties without authorization. Offshore digital EMI accounts may be rejected by Spanish counterparties, payment processors, auditors, or tax authorities where local account ownership, Spanish IBAN functionality, or resident-entity verification is required.

Payoneer Fit: High

Medium to High for payment collection, supplier payments, foreign-currency wallets, and routine cross-border transfers, provided the provider is an authorized European Economic Area payment institution or electronic-money institution, or operates lawfully through passporting or an approved local arrangement. Wise Business, Payoneer, and comparable providers should be used only within their licensed product scope. They are not substitutes for a Spanish operating bank where a local corporate IBAN, statutory capital deposit, payroll, tax direct debit, cash services, bank guarantees, commercial lending, or enhanced documentary review is required. Client funds must not be commingled with company funds, and the company must not provide regulated payment, money-remittance, deposit-taking, or foreign-exchange services to third parties without authorization. Offshore digital EMI accounts may be rejected by Spanish counterparties, payment processors, auditors, or tax authorities where local account ownership, Spanish IBAN functionality, or resident-entity verification is required.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Newly incorporated SL with no operating history, no Spanish trading counterparties, and immediate international payment activity.

Root cause: Newly incorporated SL with no operating history, no Spanish trading counterparties, and immediate international payment activity.

Defense evidence: Certificate of incorporation and current commercial-register extract; articles of association; tax identification number; director and signatory resolutions; business plan; signed customer and supplier contracts; invoices and pipeline evidence; expected monthly transaction volumes; countries, currencies, and counterparties; projected cash-flow statement; explanation of the localization and media-dubbing services.
Opaque non-resident ownership chain, nominee shareholder, trust, bearer-like arrangement, or inability to identify the natural-person ultimate beneficial owner.

Root cause: Opaque non-resident ownership chain, nominee shareholder, trust, bearer-like arrangement, or inability to identify the natural-person ultimate beneficial owner.

Defense evidence: Certified ownership chart to each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner; passports and proof of address; corporate-register extracts for all intermediate entities; shareholder agreements; powers of attorney; trust or foundation documents where applicable; beneficial-owner declarations; Spanish beneficial-ownership filing evidence where applicable; independent legal confirmation of control.
Inbound capital or shareholder funding inconsistent with stated business size, unexplained third-party funding, or funds received from a high-risk jurisdiction.

Root cause: Inbound capital or shareholder funding inconsistent with stated business size, unexplained third-party funding, or funds received from a high-risk jurisdiction.

Defense evidence: Executed shareholder loan or equity-injection agreement; board and shareholder approvals; bank statements; audited or management accounts of the funding entity; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds memorandum; tax returns or financial statements; proof of ownership of the remitting account; payment purpose; sanctions and adverse-media screening; foreign-investment filing analysis where applicable.
High-volume cross-border collections involving Latin America, offshore payment platforms, virtual assets, cash, or multiple unrelated remitters.

Root cause: High-volume cross-border collections involving Latin America, offshore payment platforms, virtual assets, cash, or multiple unrelated remitters.

Defense evidence: Customer master file; signed service agreements; invoice-to-payment reconciliation; delivery and acceptance records; platform statements; counterparty KYC; transaction-monitoring policy; sanctions-screening procedure; prohibition on cash and virtual-asset settlement unless separately approved; explanation of payment aggregators and beneficial recipients.
Mismatch between the declared ISIC 7490 localization activity and account behavior, including marketplace activity, payroll intermediation, lending, payment processing, or regulated audiovisual operations.

Root cause: Mismatch between the declared ISIC 7490 localization activity and account behavior, including marketplace activity, payroll intermediation, lending, payment processing, or regulated audiovisual operations.

Defense evidence: Detailed activity memorandum; service catalog; website and client materials; sample statements of work; staffing model; subcontractor agreements; confirmation that the company acts as principal service provider rather than payment intermediary; applicable intellectual-property and data-processing documentation; licensing analysis confirming that no sectoral authorization is required for the stated activities.
Incomplete Spanish tax, accounting, VAT, payroll, or beneficial-ownership records, or failure to explain recurring transfers to related parties.

Root cause: Incomplete Spanish tax, accounting, VAT, payroll, or beneficial-ownership records, or failure to explain recurring transfers to related parties.

Defense evidence: Spanish tax registration; VAT status; accounting ledger; annual accounts; payroll records where relevant; related-party register; transfer-pricing policy; intercompany agreements; withholding-tax analysis; board approvals; reconciled bank statements; evidence of timely tax filings and payment.
Sanctions, politically exposed person, adverse-media, fraud, corruption, or restricted-country exposure involving a customer, director, shareholder, translator, subcontractor, or beneficial owner.

Root cause: Sanctions, politically exposed person, adverse-media, fraud, corruption, or restricted-country exposure involving a customer, director, shareholder, translator, subcontractor, or beneficial owner.

Defense evidence: Risk-based enhanced due-diligence report; identity and ownership verification; sanctions-screening results; source-of-wealth evidence; contract and invoice rationale; compliance certifications; escalation and approval record; termination or blocking evidence where the relationship cannot be satisfactorily cleared.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Route equity contributions and shareholder loans from an account held in the investor's own name to the Spanish SL's account at a regulated bank or authorized EEA payment institution. Use a clear payment reference such as 'share capital contribution', 'shareholder loan under agreement dated [date]', or 'paid-in capital increase'. Before remittance, provide the bank with the executed financing instrument, corporate approvals, ownership chart, source-of-funds evidence, remitter-account proof, expected amount and currency, and any applicable foreign-investment or statistical-reporting analysis. For an incorporation or capital-increase account, obtain the bank certificate confirming deposited funds and retain the notarial and commercial-registration records. Convert only the amount needed for euro-denominated capital or operating obligations; retain foreign currency only where supported by the bank's product and treasury controls. Reconcile the bank transfer to the general ledger, shareholder register, debt schedule, tax records, and statutory accounts. Do not route capital through personal accounts, unrelated third parties, anonymous payment platforms, or pooled client-money accounts.Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments to eligible European beneficiaries and SWIFT cross-border transfers for non-SEPA currencies or jurisdictions. A SWIFT MT103 remains a standard customer-payment message, while banks are migrating to ISO 20022 payment messages; retain the bank's payment confirmation, UETR, invoice, contract, beneficiary details, and sanctions-screening record. Use commercial documentary letters of credit, standby letters of credit, documentary collections, or open-account settlement according to counterparty risk and bank availability. For a Commercial LC, define the issuing, advising, and confirming banks; governing rules such as UCP 600 where agreed; documentary requirements; Incoterms; currency; expiry; discrepancy process; and sanctions conditions. For localization services, ordinary service invoices and SEPA or SWIFT payments will usually be more proportionate than documentary trade instruments. Apply beneficiary-name screening, purpose-of-payment accuracy, related-party approval, dual authorization, segregation of duties, invoice matching, and transfer-pricing controls. Spanish banks may delay or reject payments lacking a coherent commercial purpose, complete beneficiary information, or supporting documentation.Deliverable EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF, and other bank-supported forward contracts for forecast or committed receivables and payables, documented under a treasury policy and normally confirmed under an ISDA or equivalent bank master agreement.Non-deliverable forwards for currencies with restricted convertibility or limited delivery markets, subject to bank eligibility, local-market rules, sanctions controls, suitability assessment, and applicable European market-conduct requirements.Currency swaps and cross-currency swaps for managing recurring currency funding, intercompany loans, or longer-term exposure, subject to counterparty credit limits, collateral terms, valuation controls, and EMIR-related obligations.Foreign-exchange options, collars, and structured hedges may be used only after documented risk assessment, management approval, appropriateness or suitability procedures where applicable, and full disclosure of premium, leverage, termination, collateral, and accounting consequences.SEPA and bank spot conversions for ordinary operating flows, with exposure limits, authorized counterparties, segregation of duties, independent rate verification, and monthly hedge-effectiveness and mark-to-market reporting.Treasury controls should prohibit speculative trading, require hedging of identifiable commercial exposures, maintain hedge-designation and accounting documentation where hedge accounting is intended, and address EMIR clearing, reporting, risk-mitigation, collateral, and record-retention obligations based on the company's classification and transaction profile.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Medium to High for payment collection, supplier payments, foreign-currency wallets, and routine cross-border transfers, provided the provider is an authorized European Economic Area payment institution or electronic-money institution, or operates lawfully through passporting or an approved local arrangement. Wise Business, Payoneer, and comparable providers should be used only within their licensed product scope. They are not substitutes for a Spanish operating bank where a local corporate IBAN, statutory capital deposit, payroll, tax direct debit, cash services, bank guarantees, commercial lending, or enhanced documentary review is required. Client funds must not be commingled with company funds, and the company must not provide regulated payment, money-remittance, deposit-taking, or foreign-exchange services to third parties without authorization. Offshore digital EMI accounts may be rejected by Spanish counterparties, payment processors, auditors, or tax authorities where local account ownership, Spanish IBAN functionality, or resident-entity verification is required.

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25%

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19%

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within 25 days after the end of the fiscal year (December 31 for most SL companies)

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 1 / Line 1a Net taxable income before tax deductions and incentives Non-residents report Spanish source income only; adjustments for permanent establishment if applicable Fines of €100-€1,000 per day of delay (max €25,000); criminal prosecution for evasion with fines up to 100% of evaded tax and imprisonment
Line 2 Taxable base after deductions Apply applicable deductions; non-residents may claim treaty benefits Fines of €100-€1,000 per day of delay (max €25,000); criminal prosecution for evasion with fines up to 100% of evaded tax and imprisonment
Line 3 Tax due calculation Calculate at 25% or reduced rate; withholdings credited Fines of €100-€1,000 per day of delay (max €25,000); criminal prosecution for evasion with fines up to 100% of evaded tax and imprisonment

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: €1 million annual turnover for Local File; €50 million consolidated group turnover for Master File

Economic substance scope: Spain adheres to EU Economic Substance Regulations (ESR); requires companies to demonstrate real economic activities, employees, and premises in Spain for tax purposes

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion

Statutory sanction: Criminal penalties including fines up to 100% of evaded tax, imprisonment up to 5 years, and restitution orders

Director personal liability: Piercing the corporate veil; directors face personal criminal liability, fines, and possible disqualification or travel restrictions
Failure to File Tax Return

Statutory sanction: Administrative fines €100 to €1,000 per day of delay, up to €25,000; possible criminal sanctions

Director personal liability: Personal fines and liability for corporate tax obligations; potential imprisonment in aggravated cases
Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance

Statutory sanction: Penalties of 100% of the tax adjustment; possible restitution of tax benefits

Director personal liability: Directors may incur personal liability for fraudulent conduct; fines and disqualification
Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance

Statutory sanction: Recharacterization of income; denial of deductions; fines up to €300,000 and potential criminal liability

Director personal liability: Personal responsibility for tax liabilities; possible imprisonment for fraudulent tax residency claims
